memory_update.text: The purest ABF-film and copper-resin adhesion chokepoints appear concentrated in non-US primary listings: Ajinomoto for ABF and MEC Company for copper surface treatment/adhesion chemistry. US-listed candidates are mostly adjacent yield-enablers or direct customers.

MKSI should be carried forward as the strongest US-exchange underfollowed candidate for substrate chemistry/equipment because Atotech directly touches package substrate manufacturing, copper plating, ABF-compatible processes, and electronics packaging.

ONTO and CAMT should be carried forward as yield-enabler candidates rather than materials suppliers; their survival depends on proving advanced packaging/substrate inspection revenue is material and growing with AI package complexity.

AMKR is a reference demand-pull platform for FCBGA and advanced packaging. It is useful for tracking substrate procurement constraints, but it is less directly tied to the upstream material chokepoint than MKSI, ONTO, or CAMT.

For advanced-package substrates, the key bottleneck signal from supplied evidence is beneath finished substrate makers: ABF build-up insulating film and copper-bonding / surface-chemistry inputs may be more concentrated and harder to substitute than substrate capacity alone.

US-listed pure-play exposure to ABF film and copper-bonding surface chemistry appears limited; best Layer 1B US-listed candidates may be adjacent materials, process-chemistry, and packaging-equipment companies requiring primary-source verification.

Prioritize deeper verification on MKSI / Atotech for IC substrate metallization, electroless copper, electroplating, and surface-treatment exposure, because this maps most directly to the copper-adhesion chokepoint in the supplied evidence.

ENTG and KLIC remain underfollowed US-listed hypotheses rather than confirmed node beneficiaries until filings or product literature show direct advanced-packaging substrate, ABF, FC-BGA, or OSAT/customer exposure.

ESI should be prioritized for later-layer verification because MacDermid Alpha has explicit IC substrate copper plating, copper adhesion, surface finish, RDL, panel-level packaging, and SAP exposure while ESI remains within the preferred mid-cap hunting range.

MKSI is a larger but still relevant proxy through Atotech; next work should isolate Atotech electronics/package-substrate revenue and determine whether AI/HPC substrate capacity expansions flow through MKS chemistry, equipment, or software.
CAMT is not a substrate-material supplier but may be a yield-gate candidate for advanced packaging inspection/metrology; keep as hypothesis until substrate/RDL/customer specificity is proven.

For US-listed assets, the cleanest investable mapping may be process chemistry and inspection/metrology rather than ABF film itself, because the supplied context identifies non-US or not-cleanly-US-listed leaders at the deepest build-up film and copper-bonding layers.

Layer 2 should test whether these names are genuinely underfollowed AI infrastructure beneficiaries or simply already priced specialty-materials/equipment stories by checking analyst coverage, AI/advanced-packaging revenue contribution, and management commentary frequency.

MKSI should be tracked as a US-listed Atotech proxy for IC-substrate wet chemistry, surface treatment, metallization, and plating exposure; verify actual AI/HPC substrate revenue contribution before upgrading.
CAMT is the cleanest under-USD-10B US-listed discovery candidate found in this pass for advanced packaging yield/metrology exposure, with recent OSAT orders tied to CoWoS-like AI packaging.

ENTG maps to substrate integrity, contamination control, materials handling, Cu plating deposition integrity, and yield in advanced packaging, but its revenue exposure to this exact node needs quantification.
DD has credible advanced IC-substrate materials exposure through interconnect, dry film photoresist, and copper chemistry, but corporate-separation and segment-mix verification are required.

The most direct ABF film and copper-adhesion chokepoints appear to be non-US or not cleanly investable as US-listed small/mid-cap equities; US-listed mapping is mostly through adjacent chemistry, materials handling, and inspection/metrology suppliers.

US-listed pure-play merchant suppliers of high-end sub-100nm barium titanate powder appear scarce; key powder names found in evidence are mostly Japan/China listings or private entities such as Ferro/Vibrantz.

VSH and KN are the best current US-listed underfollowed discovery-lane candidates, but both are MLCC/ceramic capacitor product hypotheses rather than confirmed high-end BaTiO3 powder chokepoint beneficiaries.
MRAAY and TTDKY should be retained as reference leaders for AI-server MLCC demand validation, not as underfollowed alpha candidates.
Next layer should separately map non-US direct powder suppliers: Sakai Chemical, Nippon Chemical Industrial, Fuji Titanium, Shandong Sinocera, and private Vibrantz/Ferro.

Sakai Chemical / SACIF should be promoted to a focused Layer 2 verification target for AI-server MLCC upstream dielectric powder exposure, with emphasis on BaTiO3 share, nano-hydrothermal capability, capacity, and customer evidence.

Nippon Chemical Industrial / NPNHF is a speculative shadow candidate due to official barium-carbonate-to-BaTiO3-for-MLCC product evidence, but US OTC ticker/liquidity and revenue materiality must be verified before inclusion in a stronger universe.

The strongest current fact pattern is downstream demand pull: Murata materials and industry reports support rising AI-server MLCC intensity; upstream powder tightness remains a hypothesis requiring supplier-level evidence.
US-listed pure-play access to high-end BaTiO3 dielectric powder appears limited; the practical US-accessible universe may rely on OTC Japanese listings plus reference ADRs for MLCC makers.

For the AI server MLCC dielectric-powder node, direct public-market exposure appears stronger in Japan-listed suppliers such as Sakai Chemical and Nippon Chemical Industrial than in clean US-listed names.
MTRN should enter the US-listed underfollowed watchlist as a hypothesis-only BaTiO3 specialty-materials candidate; survival requires proof of MLCC-grade commercial sales or capacitor-maker customers.
VSH is a second-order MLCC-component proxy, not an upstream dielectric-powder supplier; keep only if evidence appears for AI-server-qualified MLCC orders, pricing, or capacity tightness.
CBT is a stale-asset trail: historical Cabot barium titanate ceramics exposure exists, but the current product/business status must be confirmed before use in later Serenity layers.

The purest high-end BaTiO3 dielectric-powder suppliers for AI-server MLCCs appear to be non-US listed or private; US-listed exposure is mostly downstream MLCC makers, OTC ADRs, or adjacent passive-component suppliers.

Sakai Chemical 4078.JP should remain the key non-US upstream reference for future non-US universe expansion, but it should not be inserted into a US-listed candidate list unless a verifiable US-traded ordinary/ADR instrument is found.

For US-listed candidates, the correct falsification test is not simply MLCC exposure; it is evidence of high-capacitance/thin-layer MLCC demand, AI-server qualification, pricing power, capacity tightness, or dielectric-powder procurement constraints.

Vishay is the best-fit US-listed underfollowed candidate found in this pass, but its direct link to AI-server-grade thin-layer MLCCs and sub-100nm BaTiO3 powder is weak and must be treated as a hypothesis until product mix and customer exposure are verified.

POWL is the cleanest direct underfollowed US-listed candidate for data-center electrical power delivery in this pass because official 2026 releases explicitly connect record backlog and a $400M-plus order to data-center/AI power needs.

IESC should remain in the underfollowed lane as a data-center electrical/infrastructure execution beneficiary, but later layers must split data-center exposure from residential and other commercial construction exposure.
ATKR is a second-order cable-management/raceway/conduit beneficiary; exposure is plausible but less pure and needs product-level data-center revenue verification.

Hammond Power Solutions appears highly relevant for dry-type transformers and data-center backlog but is Canadian-listed rather than a primary US-listed company; evaluate separately if OTC/Canada-listed names are allowed in a later non-US pass.

Encore Wire would have been a strong US-listed cable candidate, but it became privately held after Prysmian completed the acquisition; use Prysmian only if ADR/non-US listings are permitted in a broader pass.

POWL is the cleanest direct US-listed underfollowed candidate for data-center electrical power delivery because company evidence ties it to a $400M-plus behind-the-meter data-center order and record backlog.
IESC is a strong execution-layer candidate: data-center infrastructure demand drove FY2025 Infrastructure Solutions growth and backlog expansion, but residential and other segments complicate purity.
ATKR remains a lower-confidence second-order candidate because it explicitly serves data-center electrical applications but still needs revenue-mix and backlog verification.
NVT is near the upper end of the hunting filter but has unusually relevant exposure to data-center electrical connection, protection, grounding, and power-distribution hardware.

The power-delivery chokepoint appears to include both hard goods and execution capacity: switchgear, power control rooms, conduit/cable management, connectors, grounding, enclosures, and qualified electrical project delivery.

Need a follow-up pass on US-listed transformer-specific names and regulated inputs such as transformer oil, copper/aluminum conductor capacity, specialty steel, and testing/certification bottlenecks; this pass found stronger evidence for switchgear and electrical execution than for transformer manufacturing.
POWL should be tracked as a direct switchgear/packaged-power candidate for the data_center_power_delivery node; recent evidence includes record backlog and a >$400M data-center order.
IESC should be tracked as an underfollowed electrical-infrastructure execution candidate; the key verification issue is how much backlog is truly data-center-driven and enforceable.
NVT belongs in the discovery lane despite larger market cap because Avail EPG adds switchgear, bus systems and control-building exposure that maps directly to power-delivery bottlenecks.
ATKR is a weaker, second-order conduit/cable-management hypothesis; retain for Layer 2 only if data-center revenue mix, backlog or distributor demand can be verified.
Need a separate cable/conductor pass for still-listed US or ADR names after Encore Wire's delisting; many pure cable assets are now private, foreign-listed, or absorbed by larger strategic buyers.

POWL should be tracked as a direct switchgear/power-control-room candidate for AI data-center electrical power delivery; strongest next check is backlog composition and data-center award repeatability.

IESC should be tracked as an underfollowed project-execution/electrical-contracting beneficiary; verify data-center customer mix, Communications segment growth, RPO quality, and labor/capacity constraints.

ATKR should be tracked as a cable-management/conduit hypothesis rather than a proven chokepoint; require evidence that data-center demand is material enough to offset cyclical electrical-products weakness.
nVent is useful as a non-mega reference for electrical connection/protection exposure to AI data centers and power utilities, but it is less obscure than the main discovery lane.
Need a separate pass on US-listed or OTC transformer manufacturers and foreign ADR/OTC suppliers, because many pure transformer assets appear private, non-US-listed, or foreign-listed.

BELFB should remain in the underfollowed discovery lane for thermal/power-conditioning component research; verify AI server/data-center power design wins and whether revenue is material enough to survive Layer 2.

NVT is a direct rack-level AI power/cooling infrastructure candidate, but market cap and rising AI attention mean it should be treated as a quality reference-plus-discovery bridge rather than a deeply obscure small-cap.
